prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company in St. Louis — the right company depends on your needs (residential vs. commercial), budget, the scope of work, timing, and whether your home needs lead-safe practices. I can, however, help you find the best fit and give you the criteria to choose confidently.

Quick guidance
- Decide the scope: whole house, one floor, rooms, trim/cabinet work, repairs, texture/skim-coat, color consultation.
- Check credentials: insurance, written contract, proof of liability and workers’ comp, local business license.
- Look for experience and references: recent photos/portfolio, at least 3 local references or online reviews.
- Confirm materials & prep: thorough surface prep, priming when needed, brand/type of paint (e.g., Benjamin Moore, Sherwin-Williams), cleanup.
- Ask about warranty: how they handle touch-ups and guarantees on workmanship/finish.
- Lead-safe requirement: if your house was built before 1978, confirm EPA Lead-Safe Certified renovator/painters.
- Get 3 written estimates that list scope, materials, labor, timeline, and payment terms.

Where to find and verify companies
- Google and Yelp (look at recent 4–5 star reviews)
- Angi/HomeAdvisor for insured pros and review history
- Better Business Bureau for complaints/ratings
- Nextdoor for neighborhood referrals

Questions to ask each painter
- Are you licensed/insured? Can you provide certificates?
- Do you have references or recent job photos in St. Louis?
- What surface prep is included? Is patching/plaster repair extra?
- Which paint brands and sheens do you recommend and why?
- Will you provide a written estimate and contract?
- How long will the job take? What’s your start date?
- Do you have EPA Lead-Safe certification (if needed)?

Typical cost (rough estimate)
- Interior jobs vary widely. Ballpark: $2–6 per sq. ft. overall, or roughly $300–800 per room depending on size & prep. Get specific written quotes.

If you want, I can find and compare top-rated interior painters near you. Tell me:
- ZIP code or neighborhood
- Residential or commercial
- Approximate square footage or number of rooms
- Any special needs (lead paint, crown molding, cabinets, color consult)

I’ll pull a short, vetted list (3–5) with ratings, key pros/cons, and next steps. Which neighborhood or ZIP code should I search?
